maestros.title: Master Data
maestros.subtitle: Items, suppliers, customers and families
maestros.metaTitle: Master Data | RayGold ERP - Catalog Management
maestros.metaDescription: Complete management of items, prices, structures and images of your jewelry catalog with RayGold ERP.

intro.titulo: The catalog, with weight and fineness inside it
parrafos: A jewelry item is not a reference with a price attached. It is an alloy with its fineness, a fine weight, stones with their cut and carats, and a making charge that changes depending on who does the work. RayGold's master data holds that whole structure, not a flat record with a code and a description.

Everything else follows from it. With the composition properly defined, the costing calculates itself, the price list recalculates with the day's metal and the workshop knows what material it needs before releasing the order. When the catalog is badly built, that work gets repeated by hand on every quote.

comercial.title: Sales
comercial.subtitle: Complete sales, orders and invoicing for your jewelry business
comercial.metaDescription: Total control of sales, orders, delivery notes and invoicing for jewelers with RayGold ERP.

intro.titulo: Selling gold is not selling product
parrafos: In jewelry, an invoice has to separate metal from labor. The customer may supply their own gold, the price may have been quoted at a rate from three weeks ago, and the piece may still be sitting on deposit unsold. The sales module covers the full cycle — order, delivery note, invoice — counting the grams separately.

The gold book records metal movements with customers and suppliers along with their balances, so at any moment you know who owes grams to whom. And deposits keep their own account: what went out, what has sold, and what is still out there waiting to come back or be invoiced.

fabricacion.title: Manufacturing
fabricacion.subtitle: Planning, production, materials and labor management
fabricacion.metaDescription: Planning, manufacturing map, clocking records, in-process quality control, time studies, casting, capacity and labor management for jewelers.

intro.titulo: From the released plan to the missing gram
parrafos: Manufacturing is where the margin leaks. A plan is released, moves through wax, casting, setting and polishing, and at every stage there is a weight difference someone has to account for. RayGold weighs in and out of each stage and by operator, so loss stops being one global figure at month end and gets a name, a stage and a date.

Around that sits everything else: plan release, the manufacturing map with the status of each order, the clocking records of what every operator does, the casting module with its trees, scrap and slag, and the hourly rates that turn shop-floor time into a cost you can actually pass on.

And within the route, quality and time: control points that stop a defect at the stage where it starts, with operator self-inspection and supervisor inspection, and standard times measured by time study instead of estimated, which are the ones costing and planning then use.

faq.respuesta: It never holds back work already done: the exit from a stage can always be recorded. What is held, if the control point is set to block, is entry into the next stage until the inspection is accepted. You can start in “warn only” mode and switch on blocking once the workshop is used to it.

faq.pregunta: How many time studies are needed to set a standard time?
faq.respuesta: Between 10 and 15 cycles per item, spread across several operators, days and shifts. In manual jewelry work a single measurement varies too much: below 10 cycles the time is a guide, but it is not moved to the route.

faq.pregunta: Does quality control also cover outside specialists and subcontracted workshops?
faq.respuesta: Yes. The same control point applies depending on who makes the piece: the factory, an outside specialist doing one operation or a subcontracted workshop recording from its portal. Work coming back from outside is inspected on receipt.

calidad.name: In-process quality
calidad.description: In-process quality control: a defect is stopped at the stage where it starts, not at Shipping.

parrafos: The key stages of the route have a control point. When the exit from that stage is recorded, the inspection is created automatically and, if the control blocks, the piece cannot enter the next stage until it is accepted. The exit is never blocked: the operator can always finish their work.

The right person measures: the operator for self-inspections and the supervisor for critical controls, from their pending queue. And it works the same for in-house work, for outside specialists who do a single operation and for subcontracted workshops, which record progress from their own portal.

Frequency per envelope, first piece or one in every N, and 100% inspection for orders of 1 to 5 pieces
Defects from a catalog, photos from a phone, and cause, action and owner when rejecting or reworking
Statistical process control with Cp and Cpk, alarm rules and defect Pareto by stage, operator or workshop

cronometrajes.name: Methods and times
cronometrajes.description: Standard times measured by time study, not estimated.

parrafos: Labor cost, section capacity and planning all depend on the standard time of each operation. Time studies replace estimates with measured, rated and documented times: who measured them, when and how.

Choose the item and RayGold lists its operations in route order. Time it on screen or with the printed sheet and a phone clock, and stoppages are deducted automatically. With enough cycles, the standard time is approved and moved to the route, keeping a history of the previous value.
puntos: Mean observed, normal and standard time per operation: ST = MOT × PR × (DF + 1) / 100 × (ALW + 1)
Performance rating on the 100-point scale (100 = normal pace) or other scales
Difficulty factor and allowances per workstation, with ILO reference values
The same allowances for everyone: the same operation has the same standard time, whoever does it
10 to 15 cycles per item; the most recent ones count, so the standard updates when the method improves
By operation, for maximum detail, or by section, faster for small and mid-sized workshops

ingenieria.title: Product Engineering
ingenieria.subtitle: From sketch to production: prototypes, cost and viability of every piece
ingenieria.metaTitle: Product Engineering | RayGold ERP - From sketch to production
ingenieria.metaDescription: Prototypes, versions and viability of every piece of jewelry before it is made: CAD and STL, estimated weight, stage-by-stage cost with a margin traffic light, readiness and release to production.

intro.titulo: No piece reaches the workshop without knowing whether it pays
parrafos: Before a piece is made there are sketches, waxes, 3D-printed resins, rubber molds and a first pilot cast in metal. At every step the weight, the stones and the labor hours change, and the cost with them. The Product Engineering module brings all that work together in one place and answers three questions: is the piece profitable, is it ready to make, and what has changed and why.

Each model moves through seven stages on a board, with its cost valued at each one against the target price. Once it has its design, bill of materials, route, approved prototypes, a sufficient margin and every check done, it is released, and RayGold creates the final item ready for production.

items: It is not a CAD program: the design is done in your CAD software and the STL is uploaded here.
It is not a configurator for end customers: it is the internal study of each model before it is made.
It does not duplicate the item master: the final item is created only when the version is released.

faq.pregunta: When can the cost of a new piece be calculated?
faq.respuesta: As soon as the version has a bill of materials. With the STL uploaded it is calculated from the estimated weight and, once there is a cast pilot, from the real weight. Each calculation is saved with that day’s metal price.

faq.pregunta: What happens to the money spent on prototypes?
faq.respuesta: It is added up per version and spread across the forecast units as development cost, so it becomes part of the cost of each piece.

faq.pregunta: Can a product already in production be changed?
faq.respuesta: Not directly: the released version is frozen. An engineering change order is opened with its reason and impact and, once approved, it creates a new version that goes through the stages again.

pipeline.name: From sketch to production
pipeline.description: Seven stages on a board, and the system checks what is needed before letting each card move on.

parrafos: The versions of each product are shown in columns: Sketch, Prototype, Pilot, Viability, Readiness, Released and Rejected. Cards are dragged from one stage to the next, and RayGold will not let them advance if something is missing: no pilot without a prototype, no viability without a bill of materials, no readiness without a valued cost.
Each prototype is recorded with its type (wax, 3D-printed resin, rubber mold), operator, dates, weight, hours and spend. The last approved pilot sets the real weight of the version.
puntos: Sketch: the idea, family, collection, target price and unit forecast
Prototype and pilot: physical test models and the first piece cast in metal
Viability: the full cost with the bill of materials and route, and the decision on margin
Rejected: always with a reason; if every version is rejected, the product is discarded
Each card shows cost, margin, prototypes, readiness and days in the stage

images.title: Pipeline
images.description: Versions by stage, with cost, margin, weight and days in the stage

coste.name: Cost and viability
coste.description: The cost of each version, stage by stage, against the target price.

parrafos: Every time it is calculated, RayGold makes a full valuation and saves it as is, with that day’s metal price. Valuations are never recalculated afterwards: they stay as history, you choose which one is current and you compare versions with each other.

The traffic light shows whether the margin is reached: green if it meets the target, amber up to 5 points below and red if it falls further short. In a gold piece the metal can be 90% of the cost, so a few tenths of a gram decide viability: that is why the cost can be calculated from the CAD estimated weight or from the pilot’s real weight.
puntos: Metal: weight × (1 + casting loss) × fineness × fine metal price
Stones, findings and packaging from the bill of materials, with the source of each cost
Labor from the route: hours per piece × section rate
Subcontracting: outside casting, plating or setting
Development: prototype spend spread across the forecast units
Margin against target (40% by default, configurable) and the minimum price to reach it

images.title: Cost breakdown
images.description: Metal, labor by operation and stones, with the valuation history

cad.name: CAD, STL and 3D
cad.description: Drag the file in and RayGold measures it, stores it and shows it in 3D.

parrafos: STL, 3MF and OBJ files are measured right in the browser: volume, dimensions and triangles. They are stored in the 3D Printers module ready to print, and a view of the piece is generated in the metal’s color. Photos, renders, drawings and PDFs are stored with their thumbnail.

The main STL sets the version’s volume and, with the metal’s density, gives the estimated weight. An 18 mm hoop earring with 2 mm wire has 0.1574 cm³: 2.44 g in 18K yellow gold and 1.63 g in 925 silver.
puntos: Estimated weight = STL volume × metal density
Densities and fineness for 18K and 14K gold, 925 silver and 950 platinum, configurable
3D viewer with metal reflections: rotate, zoom, show the mesh and download the file
Dimensions, volume, estimated weight and triangles below the viewer

images.title: 3D viewer
images.description: The piece from the STL: dimensions, volume, estimated weight and stones

readiness.name: Readiness and release
readiness.description: What must be ready before production, and the move to production in a single step.

parrafos: The checklist comes with a default policy and can be adjusted by family. Automatic checks are ticked by the system as soon as they are met: CAD uploaded, bill of materials, route, approved prototype and pilot, real weight and current cost. Manual checks are ticked by whoever owns them: commercial approval, pilot quality review and, where they apply, stones, photos and packaging.

When there is a current cost and every mandatory check is done, Release is enabled. In a single step RayGold creates the final item with its family, metal, karat and color, creates the new components, saves the bill of materials and stages and sets up stock. The version is frozen, with date and user.
puntos: Mandatory and optional checks, and “not applicable” for what does not apply
If something is missing, the button says exactly what: for example, 7 of 9 mandatory
Components that do not exist yet are flagged as new and created on release

images.title: Readiness
images.description: Automatic and manual checks before release

versiones.name: Versions and documents
versiones.description: Every change is a version with its reason, and every version has its customer sheet.

parrafos: A product can have several versions. A new version is created from another one with its reason and can clone its bill of materials, route and files, so alternatives are compared side by side with their costs: another metal, another thickness, other stones. A released version can no longer be edited: to change a product in production, an engineering change order is opened which, once approved, creates the new version.

Two documents are printed from the version. The customer sheet is the sales presentation, with no costs or margins, and sign-off boxes. The internal technical dossier holds the whole study: cost breakdown, bill of materials, route, prototypes, readiness and valuation history.
puntos: Change order with type, priority, requester, reason and impact analysis
Customer sheet: image, specifications, composition without amounts, optional price and sign-off
Technical dossier with prepared, reviewed and approved signatures
Both are saved as PDF to send by email

finanzas.title: Finance
finanzas.subtitle: Integrated accounting, treasury and VAT
finanzas.metaDescription: Integrated accounting, management of collections, payments, banks and financial reports for jewelers.

intro.titulo: Accounting that knows where the numbers came from
parrafos: In many workshops accounting lives in a world of its own: you invoice in one place, post it in another, and between the two sits a bridge that breaks at every close. In RayGold the journal entry is born from the operation, so from an invoice you can see its entry, and from the entry you can reach the piece that produced it.

On top of that base sit treasury, with the liquidity position and the bills issued and received; the VAT books and the collection and discount batches; and the financial statements, with a balance sheet structure defined by formulas and assigned accounts instead of rebuilt every year.

historicos.title: Historical
historicos.subtitle: Historical data and complete traceability
historicos.metaDescription: Complete access to the history of operations, movements and traceability of jewelry pieces.

parrafos: When a customer asks about a job from three years ago, or when an operation has to be justified to whoever is asking, the answer cannot depend on who happens to remember. Historical keeps the full record of operations with their original detail, and lets you find it by the criteria people actually search on.

It also holds the trail of invoicing declared under VERI*FACTU, with the record of each submission and its response. This is not a dead archive nobody opens: it is the part of the system you go to on the day you have to prove something.

inventario.title: Inventories
inventario.subtitle: Management of various inventories
inventario.metaDescription: Management of resources, stocks, movements and distributions

intro.titulo: Knowing what you have, where it is and what it is worth
parrafos: A jeweler's stock is counted in grams, in units and in carats at the same time, and it is spread across the warehouse, the workshop, the stores and outside workshops. The inventory module keeps each of those balances separately and values them, instead of collapsing everything into an average price that says very little.

Physical counts work on that basis: you count, you compare against what the system said, and the difference is recorded with its date and the person responsible. What no workshop can afford is for a discrepancy to be corrected quietly and never traced back to where it came from.

estadisticas.title: Statistics
estadisticas.subtitle: Reports and dashboards for decisions
estadisticas.metaDescription: Data analysis, custom reports and dashboards for decision making in jewelers.

intro.titulo: The workshop's numbers, without building the spreadsheet
parrafos: The information is already inside the system; the old problem is getting it out. Statistics brings together the indicators people actually look at in a workshop — what has been made, what has been sold, what it cost — in dashboards you consult directly, without asking anyone or waiting until Monday.

You can look by period, comparing months or fiscal years, or drill down to a single item to see which references move and which have been taking up space for a year. It all comes from the same data you work with every day, so there are never two versions of the same figure.

vendedores.title: Sales Reps
vendedores.subtitle: Specialized management for sales reps
vendedores.metaTitle: Sales Reps | RayGold ERP - Commercial Management
vendedores.metaDescription: Management of sales teams, commissions, targets and sales tracking for jewelers.

intro.titulo: The rep, with the catalog in hand
parrafos: A jewelry sales rep works on the road, showing pieces and taking notes at the customer's counter. They need the catalog with its images, the price at the day's metal rate and the ability to close the order right there, not a sheet of paper someone types up back at the office two days later.

The module gives the rep their own application, with the menu and calendar fitted to their route. And it gives management the other half: sales by rep and by store, commissions calculated on what has actually been collected, and a pipeline where open opportunities do not depend on anyone's memory.

ecommerce.title: E-commerce
ecommerce.subtitle: Integrated online stores and marketplaces
ecommerce.metaDescription: Integration with online store, stock synchronization and management of web orders for jewelers.

intro.titulo: The store and the workshop, on a single stock
parrafos: Selling online with the workshop's stock out of sync always ends the same way: you sell a piece that is no longer there and have to call the customer back. The e-commerce module publishes the catalog from the same items the workshop makes, with their images and specifications, and keeps quantities synchronized.

It also covers the physical side of selling: POS for the counter, distribution plans for moving product between points of sale, and cyclic counting by class. Stores and the website stop being two systems to reconcile and become two outlets of the same inventory.

impresoras3d.title: 3D Printers
impresoras3d.subtitle: Control and management of 3D printing production
impresoras3d.metaDescription: Control and management of 3D printing production for jewelry. Management of jobs, materials and configuration.

intro.titulo: The printer fleet, inside the ERP
parrafos: In most workshops 3D printing lives apart: someone knows what is printing because they walked past it, resin is estimated by eye, and nobody knows how long a machine has gone without maintenance. Print3D treats printers as one more production resource, with a record, a workload and a cost of their own.

It does not design. Geometry is still created in your CAD program and the file is still prepared in the printer's own software. What RayGold adds starts afterwards, when that file becomes shop-floor work with a machine, a material and a set of alerts behind it.

portal.title: Customer Portal
portal.subtitle: Customer access to orders, delivery notes and invoices
portal.metaDescription: Web portal for your customers to check their orders, delivery notes and invoices in real time.

intro.titulo: Let the customer look, instead of calling
parrafos: Every call asking about a job costs someone in the workshop stopping what they are doing, finding the piece and calling back. The portal gives your customers access to their own orders, with the status of each one, without anyone having to field the question.

Delivery notes and invoices work the same way: the customer logs in and sees what has been shipped, which order each piece comes from and how much has been invoiced, whenever they need it, including outside working hours. It is the module with the fewest screens in the whole system and one of the ones that gives the most hours back to the workshop.

asistenteia.title: Certifications
asistenteia.subtitle: Gemological lab submission tracking and verified reports
asistenteia.metaDescription: Gemological lab submission tracking and verified reports

intro.titulo: The certificate, tied to the stone
parrafos: A gem without its certificate and a certificate without its gem are worth the same: nothing. The certifications module tracks submissions to the gemological lab by batch — what went out, what came back and when — so no stone sits in a drawer waiting for someone to remember to chase it.

The reports that come back are stored alongside their batch and the lab that issued them. So the day a customer asks where the emerald in their ring came from, the answer gets looked up in the system and not in a folder nobody remembers filing.
